## Context / Problem

Code review has no criterion that owns correctness races. The security overlay covers only attacker-framed TOCTOU; the performance overlay covers only load-shaped concurrency (stampede, pool exhaustion); the base reviewer has no concurrency rubric. A traced corpus of four real production races in this repo shows the gap: `eclectic-spotted-barb` (detached drain child commits with a raw unlocked whole-index `git rm`+`commit`, racing locked `stage_and_commit` writers — introduced by 9ad46965bd), `fine-wisteria-solenodon` (fsck Check 3 reclaims `index.lock` via getmtime-then-remove TOCTOU — introduced by 56e130ff71), `greisen-draconian-annelid` (verify→sign reads HEAD twice; drift guard detects but closes unsigned anyway — introduced by 3938c7ed2d), and `fervid-boring-python` (CI bash retry with exponential backoff on a CAS race — introduced by ea79ecca7f). Siblings `malevolent-emigratory-umbrette` and `grassgreen-clotty-duck` are the same "unlocked twin" class, making it this codebase's modal race. Plan review already covers concurrency (T9 shared-state lifecycle, G6 mechanism correctness); code review does not.

## Approach

Add a `concurrency` Pass-1 specialist overlay to the four-pass code-review gate, following the established overlay invariants (rubric + FP guards carried in the overlay because Pass-2 is domain-blind; evidence-record contract; no model-emitted severity; empty findings expected). The rubric is lockset-first — the Eraser/RacerD "inconsistent synchronization discipline on the same resource" heuristic — because it is a citation lookup rather than an interleaving argument, so it stays reliable on less capable agents and decomposes into sub-claims the existing Pass-2 verifier disciplines already check (reachability-via-callers, prove-absence-by-searching). The overlay fires via a two-layer deterministic lexical trigger, mirroring RacerD's production precedent of a single lexical cue flipping on the analysis: a committed high-precision cross-stack token list (survey-grounded: Lu et al. ASPLOS'08, Tu et al. ASPLOS'19, RacerD trigger heuristic, CodeQL CERT packs; measured 14% fire rate over this repo's last 300 main commits), plus a project-extensible noisy tier in `.rebar/criteria_routing.json` that rebar itself dogfoods (noisy tier measured +21%; it is what makes three of the four corpus bugs trigger here). **Recall boundary (committed vs project tier), stated explicitly:** the committed high-precision tier is deliberately stack-agnostic and low-noise, so it fires only on hunks bearing an explicit synchronization primitive (thread/async/DB-lock/file-lock tokens) and DOES NOT fire on this codebase's MODAL unlocked-twin class — the raw `git rm`+`git commit` whole-index writes (`eclectic-spotted-barb`, `malevolent-emigratory-umbrette`, `grassgreen-clotty-duck`) and the `os.path.getmtime`-then-`os.remove` on `index.lock` reclaim (`fine-wisteria-solenodon`) carry no such token. Portable recall on that modal class is delivered NOT by the built-in but by the project-extensible noisy tier: a fresh project that installs the built-in overlay without adding its own `trigger_tokens` will not escalate its own git-index/lockfile unlocked-twin race, and is expected to layer its repo-specific vocabulary (as rebar itself dogfoods in the final child, e.g. `.lock`, `stage_and_commit`, `refs/reconciler/`). This is an accepted, documented recall boundary of the committed tier, not a defect — the two-tier split is the mechanism by which the built-in stays portable while this repo still catches its modal races. The overlay ships advisory (block_threshold 0.95, blocking_enabled false) per this repo's calibrate-then-flip precedent (`api-compat`, `tests`, `deletion-impact`); the blocking flip is explicitly out of scope pending calibration volume. Accepted v1 blind spots, documented rather than promised: no-twin races (the `greisen-draconian-annelid` twice-read-HEAD class) and CI-level CAS/backoff judgment (the `fervid-boring-python` class) — these are the lexical/judgment ceiling confirmed independently by the survey's blind-spot analysis.

## Child decomposition

Children deliver, respectively: the project-extensible trigger mechanism for built-in overlays (`trigger_tokens` + `applies_to` union consumed through effective routing); the overlay's Pass-1 reviewer prompt carrying the full rubric; the generic registration (overlay id, committed high-precision content trigger scanning added and removed lines, base-catalog escalation line, advisory routing entry); a standing eval spec distilled from the traced corpus (recall and no-fire families, including the deliberate check-then-act hard-FP control); and the rebar dogfood entry plus the two-layer trigger documentation. Dependencies: registration depends on the prompt existing (the workflow must never escalate to a dimension with no reviewer); the eval depends on the prompt; the dogfood depends on both the extension mechanism and the registered overlay id.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] A code-review run over a diff seeded with an unlocked-twin race surfaces a Pass-1 `concurrency` finding; checked by the standing eval `rebar prompt eval code-review-concurrency` passing its gate.
- [x] The `concurrency` overlay fires deterministically from diff content via the committed high-precision token trigger (added and removed lines), and appears in the base reviewer's overlay catalog for escalation; checked by unit tests over corpus-derived diff hunks. The committed-trigger unit tests NAME the coverage split: hunks bearing an explicit synchronization primitive (e.g. `Lock(`, `flock`, `RwLock`) fire the committed tier, while the unlocked-twin corpus hunks (raw `git rm`+`git commit`, `getmtime`+`os.remove` on `index.lock`) carry no committed token and are covered only by the project noisy tier — so the committed-tier test asserts the sync-primitive hunks fire and the project-tier config-effect test (AC#4) asserts the unlocked-twin vocabulary fires only under project routing.
- [x] A project can extend a built-in overlay's trigger vocabulary and `applies_to` globs through `.rebar/criteria_routing.json` without code changes; checked by unit tests with a project-overlay fixture.
- [x] rebar's own `.rebar/criteria_routing.json` carries the noisy-tier concurrency vocabulary as the documented worked example, and the two-layer trigger design is documented in `docs/llm-framework.md`; checked by a config-effect test proving a project token (`index.lock`) triggers the overlay under this repo's effective routing but not under committed-only routing.
- [x] The committed routing entry for `concurrency` is advisory (`block_threshold` 0.95, `blocking_enabled` false); checked by a unit assertion on `threshold_for("concurrency")`.
